annotations.text:
Detour Reports as shipped — v1.5.109, merged in PR #174

1. Status is a tab bar with live counts, opening on ACTIVE. It replaced a status dropdown AND a separate Show/Hide history toggle that decided the same thing twice. Each count reflects what the other filters already allow.
2. Search is the full-width control; the other five filters sit behind a Filters button with a count badge, and every applied one is a removable chip. Clear filters keeps the status tab.
3. Fifteen columns became seven plus a disclosure control. Avail number, path, workflow, reason, severity, source and provenance moved into the expanded record — the CSV export still carries all 51 fields.
4. The expanded record is a labelled definition grid instead of a stack of dim sentences.
5. Rows disclose through a real button with aria-expanded, so the record is keyboard-reachable.

The detour data on these artboards is invented sample content — plausible MVTA corridors, not real records.

Export preview — click Export on the artboard

The button opens a preview before anything downloads: the file name, the row and column counts, the filters it was taken under, and the rows themselves, with Download CSV beside Open in browser (the same export rendered as a standalone HTML page in a new tab).

The artboard shows the first eight of 51 columns; the real dialog scrolls sideways through all of them. Preview and file are generated from one table (detourExportTable), so they cannot drift apart.

Legacy spreadsheet history: removed

The whole subcard is gone — the imported-rows table, the Show/Hide toggle, and the CSV/JSON upload control that lived inside it.

Worth knowing: that upload was the ONLY way to import retired-tracker rows. Removing the panel removed the import path from the console. The rows and POST /detours/historical-imports stay; nothing is deleted.
